answers.core: This would add a new `mouse_filter` type to Control, which can't be done by an add-on, and this has to do with the Control node and input event systems which are built-in.
answers.workaround:
Yes, but the method to do this is not ideal. Right now, if you want input to continue downward, you have to set the Control node's `visible` to `false` so that it won't be registered when the event is run again, run the same input event again using `Input.propagate_event()`, wait one frame for the input event to have run, then set the Control node's `visible` back to `true` so it can take input again.

Here is an example using left and right click:
```gdscript
func _gui_input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
	if event is InputEventMouseButton:
		match event.button_index:
			BUTTON_RIGHT:
				accept_event()
				# Do stuff
			BUTTON_LEFT:
				visible = false
				Input.parse_input_event(event)
				yield(get_tree(), "idle_frame")
				visible = true
```

title: Control `mouse_filter` mode that behaves like `Ignore` when mouse input is not accepted
